text: To bungle something is to do a job clumsily and mess it up. Rentokil's takeover of Terminix went so badly that investors sued.
Recurring means happening again and again on a schedule. Customers pay for regular visits, so the money keeps coming back.
To purge something is to get rid of it completely. People will pay to purge bed bugs from their homes.
Rubbish is the British word for trash or garbage. The Economist is a British magazine, so it uses British words.
A pesticide is a chemical that kills pests like insects. Bed bugs are getting harder to kill because they have become resistant to it.
Here resistance means the bugs have changed over time so the poison no longer works well on them. It is not about fighting back on purpose.
Termites are small insects that eat wood. They can slowly ruin the wooden frames of houses.
To chew through something is to eat a path into it bit by bit. Termites do this to wood.
Pest control is the job of getting rid of unwanted animals and insects like rats, bed bugs and termites. The people and companies that do it are pest-controllers.
Buzzing is the sound bees make, but it also means busy and full of energy. The writer is joking that the industry is busy even as these companies are not.
A share price is what one tiny piece of a company costs right now. When it falls, investors think the company is worth less.
A flagship is the most important or best-known one of a group. Orkin is the main service of Rollins.
Hatched usually means coming out of an egg. Here it means a business was started, which is a fitting joke for a bug story.
An immigrant is a person who moves to a new country to live there. Otto Orkin came from Latvia to the United States.
Latvia is a small country in northern Europe, beside the Baltic Sea.
Poison is a substance that harms or kills living things. Orkin first sold rat poison.
A fluid is anything that flows, like water or liquid medicine. Rentokil was a liquid that was put on wood.
Westminster Hall is a very old, huge building next to Britain's Parliament in London. Its great wooden roof is hundreds of years old.
Deathwatch beetles are insects that tunnel into old wood and make tapping sounds. They can damage old roofs.
Parliamentarians are the people who work in a country's Parliament, the group that makes its laws.
To dominate is to be the biggest and strongest in an area. These two firms have led pest control for a century.
Revenue is all the money a business takes in from selling things, before paying its costs.
A takeover is when one company buys another and takes control of it.
Investors are people or groups who put money into companies hoping to earn more later.
To sue is to take someone to court to say they did something wrong and should pay for it.
Stunk literally means smelled bad. Here it means growth has been very poor, like a bad smell that stays.
To be plagued is to be troubled again and again by something bad.
An excuse is a reason someone gives to explain why something went wrong, often to avoid blame.
Technicians are workers trained to do hands-on technical jobs. Here they visit homes to treat pests.
Earnings expectations are the profits experts predict a company will make. Missing them means the company did worse than predicted.
In business a quarter is three months of the year, not a quarter coin. Companies report their results every quarter.
Creeping means moving slowly and quietly. The threats are growing slowly and are not yet easy to see.
Private equity firms collect money from rich investors and use it to buy whole companies, often to sell later for profit.
A defensive business keeps earning even when times are hard. People still need bed bugs removed even if money is tight.
The economy is all the buying, selling and making of things in a country.
To subscribe is to sign up to pay regularly for a service.
An infestation is when lots of pests, like rats or bugs, take over a place.
Claws are the sharp nails of animals. Here the writer says firms keep their claws stuck into customers, meaning they hold on tightly.
To quadruple is to become four times as big.
To gobble up is to eat fast and greedily. Here it means buying small companies quickly.
To merge is to join two things into one. Companies merge to become bigger.
Incumbents are the companies that already hold the top place in a business. The new competitors are challenging them.
Market share is the slice of all the sales in a business that one company gets. A drop from 53% to 51% means it sells a little less of the total.
A scourge is something that causes great trouble or suffering, like a plague.
AI stands for artificial intelligence, computer programs that can answer questions and do tasks that seem smart.
Chatbots are computer programs you can talk with by typing.
Search engines, like Google, are websites that help you find things on the internet.
To scrape a website is to copy information from it automatically with a program.
Reddit is a website where people post and talk about all kinds of topics, including reviews.
Rosier means more cheerful and positive, like looking through rose-colored glasses.
To inspire rage is to make people very angry.
A rodent is a small gnawing animal like a rat, mouse or squirrel.
Orkin is a big American pest-control company that began in 1901.
Terminix is a large pest-control company, now owned by Rentokil.
Data centres are large buildings full of computers that store information and run AI. Neighbors sometimes object to them being built nearby.
A rat race is a tiring competition where everyone is rushing to get ahead. Here it is a pun, since the story is about rats.
Rollins is the American company that owns Orkin.
Rentokil is a British pest-control company that began in the 1920s.
